title: Checking a developer in Dushanbe: the project, block and terms
excerpt: Check the official project map, compare documents and question the seller. A registry entry does not replace reviewing the agreement and payment terms.
contentHtml:
Substantively checked and updated on 16 October 2026.

Check the company, particular project, relevant block and offered apartment separately. A development name matching an advertisement does not establish which documents cover the selected building or what obligations the seller accepts.

Find the correct project and block

On the official МЕЪМОР.pro map, compare the commissioning entity, decision number, specific block and published permits. Consider the stated project status. The department directs buyers to seek final confirmation and does not take responsibility for payments between buyer and company. Clarify uncertain records with the department.

Compare advertising with documents

Ask the seller for project documents and identify the contracting organisation. Compare the parties, designated use, block, floor and apartment reference. Resolve discrepancies through explanation and evidence rather than a sales representative’s verbal promise. Give copies to your chosen professional for checks relevant to the transaction.

Review the price and payment schedule

Clarify the full price, currency, price adjustment terms, schedule, possible extra payments and consequences of late payment. Obtain a written total for any proposed instalments. A low price does not establish unlawful construction, nor does a high one guarantee completion. Agree a suitable payment process with the bank and relevant professional.

Distinguish construction from handover

Record the demonstrated stage and what must be ready at handover. Agree inspection arrangements, included finishes, how defects are reported and response times. Where timing, connections or finishes matter to your decision, request that the applicable agreement records the commitments.

Keep the outcome of the checks

Record the date of checking the register, document references and unresolved questions. Keep the agreed contract, appendices and payment evidence. Discuss changes or delays with a professional reviewing your agreement. This article sets no universal penalty and does not certify all catalogue properties as clear of legal issues.

faq.q: Is appearing in the register enough?
faq.a: No. The specific block, documents and contracting parties still need to match. A map entry does not establish fulfilment of financial obligations or all sale terms.

faq.q: Does an unusually low price prove a document problem?
faq.a: No. It is a reason to investigate, but a legal conclusion requires documents and transaction terms rather than price alone.
